limitations: Memory evidence describes local stores, not context injection. Claude worktree-shared roots and directory environment overrides are not reconstructed. Declared custom locations are inspected without asserting effective settings. Codex database schemas are internal and may change; thread attribution and history counts are bounded. Generated memory files remain shared host data.
Current local declarations are a snapshot, not proof of configuration used by historical sessions.

Codex exec-policy rule files are counted, not interpreted. Vendor diagnostic logs, task queues and automation state are not interpreted. Persisted tool-output files and historical file snapshots are not independently imported.

Project trust, command-line overrides, remote managed policy, additional directories, memory imports, nested instruction files, and runtime plugin overrides are not reconstructed. Local managed policy files are read as declarations; precedence is not evaluated. Project declarations are not claimed effective.

Custom commands, prompts and output styles are local definitions; built-in and account-side commands are not enumerated. claude.ai connector names come from a local client record, not current account state.

Plugin cache presence is not enablement; cached versions may be inactive. Configured enablement is separate from selected version and runtime loading. Remote installs, CLI plugin directories, marketplace overlays, and unsupported manifest formats may be missing. Hook command basenames can be ambiguous.
